clue.text: Report of French pirate in the Dover area

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: the pirate word is placed inside the area letters, as the clue says

parts.note: Dover is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
to pirate is to copy unlawfully, to crib

explanation.surface: An account of a French buccaneer operating around the port of Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pirate' looks like a noun; here it is a verb meaning to copy. Dover is a Channel port in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account of something is to report on it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Abandon the big noise framing a pig

indicators.note: the noise word surrounds the pig word, like a frame round a picture

parts.note: a din is a big noise
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Leave a racket going around a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to reject or cast them off, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Point or line causing distress

parts.note: a point of the compass, here south, S
taken as written
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A small detail or a queue can be upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief and sadness are forms of mental distress; a synonym.

clue.text: The extent of the cooking facilities?

definitions.meaning: the scope or spread of something
a kitchen stove with hotplates and oven

explanation.definitionFit: Range means scope or reach, and is also an old-style kitchen stove.

clue.text: Domestic staff could be subtler!

indicators.note: the word subtler could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A remark that household servants might show more finesse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' tells you to rearrange SUBTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Butlers are the senior male servants in a household.

clue.text: Miscalculate with charge

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and means together with

explanation.surface: Getting a sum wrong and being accused of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge in the sense of a task one is sent to do; an errand is such a commission.

clue.text: Check the impulse to give support

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
force is an impelling push, an impulse

explanation.surface: Restrain the urge so as to help someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen or prop up is to give support; a synonym.

clue.text: Bloomers no seamen would make

indicators.note: the letters of no seamen would make a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Underwear that sailors would refuse to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would make' signals rearranging NO SEAMEN. 'Bloomers' looks like underwear; it means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are flowering plants, things that bloom.

clue.text: Set off for school, filling in time

indicators.note: the school word fills the middle of the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leaving for school, with a gap in the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like departing for school, but it means to explode; Eton is the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to explode it; a synonym.

clue.text: Odd characters are sent by a piece of music

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Strange people are sent out by a musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges ARE SENT plus the A at the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenata is a type of cantata or serenade, an instrumental or vocal composition.

clue.text: Most superior if going back home

indicators.note: the word if is read in reverse direction

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: The best if one returns to one's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Finest is the superlative of fine, meaning of best quality.

clue.text: Cuff cut short

definitions.meaning: a cuff is a light blow with the hand
to trim or shorten with shears

explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a smack round the ear, and to clip is to trim.

clue.text: Sort of bread unsuitable for sandwiches?

definitions.text: Sort of bread unsuitable for sandwiches?

parts.words: Sort of bread unsuitable for sandwiches
parts.note: a sandwich is a snack, so a bread suited to a full sit-down repast would not suit one

explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal bread is made from unrefined flour; the clue jokes that it makes a complete repast, not a snack.

clue.text: Gone with the drift north

parts.note: a flow is a drift or current

explanation.surface: Evokes the film Gone with the Wind, swapped for a northern drift.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that have flown have departed; a synonym.

clue.text: May be drawn or may be lost

indicators.note: the word lost may be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Something can be drawn, or it can be mislaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are drawn to decide something by chance.

clue.text: The man working his fingers to the bone?

definitions.text: The man working his fingers to the bone?

parts.words: The man working his fingers to the bone
parts.note: the idiom for toiling hard, read literally as a practitioner pressing on a patient's skeleton

explanation.definitionFit: This practitioner treats patients by manipulating bones and joints.

clue.text: A number drink outside a bad sign

indicators.note: the drink word goes round the number word

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone drinking outside, an ill omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like a vague quantity but means one specific number.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen of trouble is a portent.

clue.text: Conflicting in truth over unpaid debts

indicators.note: in a down entry the first word sits over the second

parts.note: a fact is a truth
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: Disputing the facts about outstanding debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Factious means given to dissension and party strife.

clue.text: Food in the can

definitions.meaning: in prison, British slang; doing ... means serving a jail sentence

explanation.walkthrough: 'The can' is slang for prison; porridge is British slang for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: Oat breakfast cereal, and British slang for time served in jail.

clue.text: Messenger or porter enveloping mail

indicators.note: the beer word wraps around the mail word

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an ale
post is mail

explanation.surface: A courier or a doorman wrapping letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a doorman or carrier; it is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostle comes from the Greek for one sent out, a messenger.

clue.text: Looked for a little money, edging around

indicators.note: only a little of the words money edging is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Searched for small change around the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyed means looked at, watched.

clue.text: Leaf-damaging insect

indicators.note: damage to the word leaf breaks its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A bug that chews leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small jumping parasitic insect.

clue.text: Delivers first-class climbing plant

parts.note: to deliver is to free or set free

indicators.note: in a down entry the first-class letters climb, reading upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class

explanation.surface: Releases a top-grade creeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns A1 (A and the figure one, as I) upwards to IA. 'Climbing plant' looks like a creeper, but 'climbing' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant grown from corms.

clue.text: One's among others in dispute

indicators.note: the one's letters are placed among the others letters

parts.note: the rest means the others
one is I, and 's is is: I IS

explanation.surface: One person stands among the rest in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I plus 's read as IS, rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or contest, so to dispute.

clue.text: Go near, distracting the beast

indicators.note: distracting jumbles the words go near into another order

explanation.surface: Approach, distracting the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of Asia, an animal.

clue.text: Turning corrupt, so forming a body

indicators.note: turning the corrupt word round makes it read backwards

parts.note: to rot is to corrupt or decay
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going bad, so forming a physical form.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body.

clue.text: Rosemary is invariably gullible

parts.note: ever means always, invariably
green means naive, inexperienced

explanation.surface: A woman called Rosemary is always easily fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosemary' looks like a woman's name; it is the shrub, which keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an example of a plant that keeps its foliage year-round.

clue.text: Delighted with English clearing

parts.note: glad means pleased, delighted

explanation.surface: Pleased with an English woodland gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A glade is an open space in a forest.

clue.text: Gold trade-a very tough business

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: Dealing in gold is a hard line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful, trying experience.

clue.text: A quarter saw the testing

parts.note: south, S, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A district witnessed the examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see; it is a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaying is testing metal or ore for its purity.

clue.text: Scan an article and get all steamed up

parts.note: to scan is to look at, see
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Read an article and become furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil with anger, to fume.

clue.text: A person sorry to find males among following

indicators.note: the males word is placed inside the following word

parts.note: later means following, subsequently
men are males

explanation.surface: Someone regretful finds men in the procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a procession; here it means coming afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamenter is one who mourns or expresses grief.
